title: Helm Therapeutics — network & residency topology POC scoping
topics: benchmarks: QPS / p95 latency / token throughput
summary: POC scoping call to define network topology (peering v PrivateLink), residency requirements, benchmark plan and success metrics. Customer wants strictly no egress outside EU region for inference; interested in dedicated/private deployment. Agreed on 4-week pilot: infra setup, bench runs, tuning, and report. Action items: Redwood to send peering runbook, security pack, and draft benchmark script; Helm to provide VPC CIDRs, test prompts, and sample traffic profile.
header:
Date: 2027-11-03 16:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Duarte (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (CTO, Helm), Liam O'Connor (Head Infra), Priya Rao (Security), Noah Kim (ML Infra), Eva Zhang (Procurement)
Recording: fireflies.ai export
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intro — Maya Chen, account exec. Ravi and Carlos are gonna handle the deep infra details.
[00:12] Sofia (Helm CTO): Hi all, thanks. We're trying to scope a short POC to validate private networking and that inference traffic never leaves eu-west-1. Need to understand options, cost, and what benchmarks you can run.
[00:25] Ravi (Redwood SE): Great. high level options are VPC peering, PrivateLink, or an isolated private deployment (private control plane). Each has tradeoffs: peering is simpler for lower-latency egress, PrivateLink gives endpoint isolation and no route table changes but adds NAT complexity, and private deployment is the most isolated but needs more ops.
[00:45] Liam (Head Infra): For us the non-negotiable is no egress outside EU. Also we have strict firewall egress rules — only specific subnets can reach Redwood endpoints. We prefer VPC peering if possible because it maps cleanly into our current transit architecture.
[01:05] Priya (Security): Also SOC2/audit-wise, we need KMS integration and proof of no-data leakage. Do you provide an HSM-backed KMS option and audit logs for inference request metadata?
[01:18] Carlos (Redwood SE): Short answer: yes to KMS integration and audit logging. HSM-backed KMS typically available via customer-managed KMS in your cloud. We'll attach logs to the private control plane. Note: some field names in the logs may be redacted for PII by default, we can configure retention.
[01:34] Noah (ML Infra): On workload sizing — expected throughput is around 120 infer/sec peak for a batch of 4k token prompts, average ~35 infer/sec outside peaks. Typical prompt distribution: 60% short (<=256 tokens), 30% medium (256–1024), 10% long.
[01:55] Ravi: Good detail. For benchmarking we'll want the actual test prompts and a synthetic traffic profile. Our suggested bench: 50 concurrent connections, ramp to 120 qps over 5 minutes, sustained 15 minutes, run 3 iterations. Collect p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit/miss rates.
[02:18] Sofia: p95 targets? We want sub-300ms for short prompts end-to-end.
[02:24] Ravi: Sub-300ms p95 for short prompts is realistic on a dedicated A100/ H100 profile with proper batching and prefix caching. For medium and long prompts the p95 will increase — we expect 800ms–1.2s for medium on the same profile. We'll include fallbacks to a lower-cost variant if you want to test cost-latency tradeoffs.
[02:44] Liam: Cost is definitely a consideration. Can Redwood provide quantized model variants?
[02:50] Maya: Yes, we can recommend quantization and batching profiles via Redwood Optimize. For the POC we'll show two profiles: high-performance (higher cost) and cost-optimized (8-bit quantized).
[03:03] Priya: Compliance — besides KMS, we need SSO (SAML) integration for console access and role-based access control so only select engineers can trigger benchmark runs.
[03:14] Carlos: SAML SSO and RBAC are supported. We'll share the SAML metadata and mapping guidance. Also we can create a restricted role for bench execution and a separate read-only role for audit.
[03:30] Eva (Procurement): Timeline questions — we need pricing to run the pilot within our budget window this quarter.
[03:36] Maya: We'll share a pilot pricing estimate. Typical 4-week POC billing is usage-based with a small onboarding fee for private networking setup.
[03:44] Sofia: Can you walk through the network topologies again? We want to hear explicit recommended approach for our on-prem VPN plus cloud transit.
[03:52] Ravi: Sure. Option A: VPC peering into a Redwood-managed VPC in eu-west-1. Pros: direct routes, lower latency, easier to inspect traffic. Cons: route table management and limits on peering across accounts/regions.
[04:08] Ravi: Option B: AWS PrivateLink — we provision a service endpoint in your account and traffic stays within AWS backbone but traverses endpoint ENIs; pros: no peering routes, easier IAM scoping; cons: slightly higher latency and potential egress cost differences.
[04:25] Ravi: Option C: Private deployment — we deploy control and data plane into your VPC or private account. Highest isolation, you manage more infra, longer lead time.
[04:39] Liam: Given our transit setup and existing peering constraints, Option A (peering) is preferred. But we need to confirm peering limits with our network team; if we hit limits we'll fallback to PrivateLink.
[04:52] Maya: Good. We'll prepare both runbooks. We'll also include a checklist for egress firewall ports and IP ranges.
[05:00] Sofia: Benchmark specifics: will the benchmark include tokenization and post-processing overhead (we call that 'end-to-end')?
[05:07] Carlos: Yes, our standard bench captures end-to-end latency: client-to-response including tokenization, model inference, and post-processing. We'll also run a raw runtime test that isolates model inferencing layer (no network) so you can see host-level performance.
[05:22] Noah: For long prompts we care about KV cache behavior — especially for chat workloads. Can you measure KV cache warm/cold case?
[05:30] Ravi: Absolutely; we'll run warm-cache and cold-cache iterations and report cache hit rates and token throughput. We'll note how much latency delta the KV cache contributes.
[05:38] Priya: Audit/retention: we need 12 months of request metadata retention and the ability to export logs for audits. Is that configurable?
[05:45] Carlos: Yes, retention is configurable. We can enable 12 months retention in the private control plane and provide an export job to your S3.
[05:52] Sofia: Data residency — we need evidence that models and request logs never leave eu-west-1. How do you enforce region-locking?
[05:59] Ravi: Our routing policy can pin requests to eu-west-1 model instances. For private deployments the control plane and model runtime are provisioned in your region. We'll provide network traces and attestations as part of the POC report.
[06:12] Eva: Any legal hoops? We may need a DPA addendum for the pilot.
[06:16] Maya: We'll have legal attach a limited-scope DPA and a pilot addendum. We'll loop in Contracts once you confirm the POC start date.
[06:24] Sophia: (laugh) Sofia: Sophia? sorry, Sofia — mixing names.
[06:28] (laughter)
[06:36] Maya: Let's nail down success criteria — what must happen for Helm to call the POC successful?
[06:41] Sofia: 1) p95 <300ms for short prompts end-to-end in eu-west-1, 2) no data egress outside EU, 3) audit logs available and KMS integration validated, 4) cost projection that fits our budget (within 20% of target), 5) a benchmark report and runbook for production rollout.
[07:01] Maya: Good crisp criteria — we'll formalize that in the POC doc.
[07:06] Liam: On resource sizing — suggest GPU profile. What would you recommend for the observed loads?
[07:12] Ravi: For 120 inf/sec peaks with mixed prompt lengths, a pool of 4 x H100 (or 6 x A100) in a dedicated cluster with autoscale to handle bursts should meet latency targets with batching. If you want a cost-optimized variant, we can test 8-bit quantized LLMs on 4 x A100s with slightly higher p95. We'll include a capacity plan with headroom.
[07:36] Noah: Are warmup caches persistent across restarts? We have auto-restart policies in our infra.
[07:41] Carlos: Cache persistence depends on the runtime; KV cache is in-memory but we support snapshotting to speed warm starts for some model families. We'll note behavior per model in the report.
[07:55] Priya: Encryption in transit and at rest? We need TLS mutual auth for peering and encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys.
[08:02] Carlos: TLS in transit is default; for peering traffic you can enable mTLS between your load balancer and our endpoints. At rest we support customer-managed KMS keys.
[08:12] Eva: Scheduling — what's the earliest start date? We want to start next week if possible.
[08:17] Maya: We can tentatively start next Tuesday (2027-11-09) pending your network tickets and SSO/KMS info. Setup usually takes 3–5 business days.
[08:26] Sofia: Sounds tight but doable. We'll prioritize.
[08:30] (several people typing)
[08:48] Maya: To make the bench actionable we'll need: VPC CIDRs, any restrictive NACLs, list of allowed egress ports, sample prompts and expected traffic profile. Also a small test account or AWS role to create peering/endpoint is ideal.
[09:05] Liam: We'll provide CIDRs and open a support ticket for peering approval. Also we'll provide a pre-authorized role.
[09:12] Mario: (background)
[09:18] Maya: Any blockers from procurement on the pilot?
[09:21] Eva: Need an internal PO and a short statement of work. I'll take Redwood's pricing and SOW and loop legal.
[09:28] Maya: We'll produce an SOW and pilot estimate.
[09:32] Carlos: For the benchmark scripts we'll use your prompt set and augment with our synthetic load generator to simulate concurrency patterns. We'll capture detailed telemetry: latency histograms, token-level timings, GPU counters, and network egress volumes.
[09:50] Noah: Will you include a regression test for quality? We care about generation fidelity when you switch to quantized models.
[09:56] Ravi: Yes we'll run a small evaluation set and compute quality deltas (ROUGE/BLEU-like metrics and human spot checks). We can also run an eval harness you provide.
[10:08] Priya: For audit we want a signed attestation at the end of the POC that states all controls were adhered to.
[10:14] Maya: We can provide a technical attestation and logs export; legal can generate the compliance attestation.
[10:21] Sofia: Ok let's go through the immediate next steps — what does Redwood own and what Helm owns?
[10:26] Maya: Redwood: prepare peering + PrivateLink runbooks, security pack (SAML/KMS/audit), pilot pricing and SOW, and draft benchmark scripts. Helm: share VPC info, sample prompts, designate AWS role, and internal approval for start date.
[10:40] Sofia: Agreed.
[10:43] Maya: Anything else?
[10:45] (silence)
[10:48] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with docs and a calendar invite for kickoff.
[10:52] (meeting ends)
